text.text: An employee has violated a written or established workplace policy. The response depends on severity, whether it was a first offense, and whether the policy has been applied consistently.

• An employee who used company equipment for personal business in violation of the IT policy.
• Someone who shared confidential client information externally without authorization.
• A team member who bypassed a safety protocol resulting in a near-miss incident.
• An employee who falsified time records.
• Someone who violated the social media policy by posting about a client.
• A manager who failed to follow the required approval process for a significant purchase.
• An employee caught accessing systems or files outside their authorized scope.
• Someone who violated the workplace conduct policy through inappropriate language or behavior.
Gather and preserve these records as you work through the check.

1. Save a copy of the policy that was violated, including the version and date the employee signed or acknowledged it.
2. Write a factual description of the violation: what happened, when, who observed it, what evidence exists.
3. Document how you became aware of the issue and any investigation steps you took.
4. Note whether this is a first offense or whether there is a prior discipline history.
5. Record any mitigating explanation the employee offered.

elements.text: You can attach files and links securely from the completed assessment before submitting it to HR.

text.text: Watch for: Selective enforcement. If you discipline one employee for a violation but have tolerated the same behavior from others, you create disparate treatment risk.
Contact HR: If you are not certain the policy applies clearly to this situation, or if similar behavior has been overlooked in the past — contact HR before taking action.
